text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Iraq agrees to increase oil deliveries to Jordan to meet increased winter demand. Iraqi Trade Minister Mohammed Mehdi Saleh expected in Amman today for talks over 1997 protocol agreement.
- Indonesian President Suharto in Amman tomorrow to meet King Hussein and sign economic cooperation accords.
- King Hussein says the alternative to peace will have heavy consequences. The only way to guarantee security is mutual respect, trust and understanding.
- Egyptian presidential adviser Osama el-Baz tells Amman seminar on Middle East that a Palestinian state will come about, whether the extremists in Israel like it or not.
- King Hussein expected to issue amnesty in next few days for some detainees.
- Parliamentary deputy Toujan Feisal sentenced to two months in jail and fined 6,000 dinars ($8,500) for slander.
- Japan offers Jordan a $12 million grant to improve water distribution, Planning Minister Khalaf says.
- Higher Education Minister Ensour says government is within sight of finalising new laws as part of its economic reform programme.
- Supply Minister Sobar says government will distribute 1997 ration cards next week to needy people.
- King congratulates U.S. President Clinton for his re-election, Russian President Yeltsin for successful operation.
